Federal Corporation vs Ontario Corporation

Both file the same federal T2 at the same price. What changes is the registry, the annual return and where that annual return is filed.

Start Nil T2 Filing NOWDate the Annual Return

Quick Answer

Both file the same federal T2 at the same price. Where a corporation was incorporated does not change the return, the schedules or the fee. What it changes is the registry that holds the record and the annual return that goes with it, which is a separate filing from the T2 and is not covered by this fee. Either way the nil T2 is $300.00 plus HST per tax year, signed on Form T183CORP and transmitted the same way.

Nil T2 filing in Canada › Nil T2 filing price › Nil T2 filing cost › Federal Corporation vs Ontario Corporation

Written and reviewed by Sharad Gondaliya, CPA (Ontario), CPA Ontario Membership 61040184.

Last reviewed: November 4, 2026

One T2, Two Registries

Corporate income tax is federal. A corporation incorporated in Ontario and a corporation incorporated federally file the same T2, on the same deadline, with the same schedules. Nothing about a quiet year changes because of where the certificate came from.

What does change is the registry obligation sitting alongside it. Filing the T2 does not satisfy an annual return, and filing an annual return does not satisfy the T2. A corporation needs both, every year, for as long as it exists, and the annual return is not part of this service.

This comparison sets two of our own filing routes against each other and names no other provider. Where a comparison on this site does name one, it states that provider’s published prices and published features only.

The Annual Return Is a Separate Obligation

Whichever registry holds the corporation, the annual return sits outside the T2:

  • An Ontario corporation files an annual return confirming its registered office address, its directors and its officers. It carries no tax and no payment.
  • Since October 2021 that Ontario filing goes through the Ontario Business Registry. Until 2021 it was filed alongside the T2, which is why older advice still says otherwise.
  • A federal corporation files an annual return with Corporations Canada, at the fee that registry sets.
  • A federally incorporated corporation operating in Ontario files both. Federal incorporation does not remove the provincial obligation.
  • Whether a province collects its own corporate tax turns on a permanent establishment there, not on where the corporation was incorporated.
  • Quebec and Alberta each collect their own corporate tax, so CO-17 and AT1 are separate returns. They are not part of the federal T2 and are not covered by this fee.

Neither annual return is included in nil T2 filing, and missing one is not fixed by filing the other. They are different filings, to different bodies, on different dates.

The annual return versus tax return checker separates the two, the provincial return requirement checker takes the permanent establishment question, the federal annual return anniversary calculator dates the Corporations Canada filing, and the complete guide to provincial and federal annual returns sets out the fees and the dates.

Frequently Asked Questions

Does a federal corporation pay more for a nil T2?

No. The fee is $300.00 plus HST per tax year for either corporation. Where it was incorporated does not change the return or the price.

Is the T2 different for an Ontario corporation?

No. Corporate income tax is federal, so both file the same T2 on the same deadline with the same schedules.

What is the difference then?

The registry. A federal corporation is on the Corporations Canada register and an Ontario corporation is on the Ontario Business Registry, and each owes that registry an annual return.

Is the annual return included in the fee?

No. The annual return is a registry filing, not a tax return, and it is not part of nil T2 filing.

Does filing the T2 satisfy the annual return?

No, and the reverse is also true. Filing an annual return does not satisfy the T2. A corporation needs both, every year, for as long as it exists.

What does the Ontario annual return actually report?

The registered office address, the directors and the officers. It carries no tax and no payment.

Where is the Ontario annual return filed?

Through the Ontario Business Registry. Until 2021 it was filed alongside the T2, which is why older guidance still describes it that way.

What does a federal corporation file instead?

An annual return with Corporations Canada, at the fee that registry sets. The complete guide to provincial and federal annual returns carries the current figure.

I am federally incorporated but operate in Ontario. Which do I file?

Both. The Corporations Canada annual return and an Ontario filing. Federal incorporation does not remove the provincial obligation.

Does incorporating federally avoid provincial corporate tax?

No. What decides whether a province collects its own corporate tax is a permanent establishment in that province, not where the corporation was incorporated.

What about Quebec and Alberta?

Quebec and Alberta each collect their own corporate tax, so CO-17 and AT1 are separate returns. They are not part of the federal T2 and are not covered by this fee.

Do the GIFI schedules differ by registry?

No. The schedules follow what sits on the corporation’s books, not the registry that holds its record.

Is the deadline different?

The T2 is due six months after the fiscal year-end for either corporation. The annual returns run on their own dates, which are not the T2 deadline.

Does the corporation number differ?

A federal corporation and an Ontario corporation are identified on different registers, which is one reason the two annual returns cannot be filed in place of each other.

Which tool should I run first?

The annual return versus tax return checker, which separates what this service covers from what the registry wants.
